Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-07-16 | AAPL | Overweight | -3.5% | -1.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL — own the reacceleration and the fresh China AI catalyst, but stage the entry and cap pre-Q3 size instead of chasing the $333 record print. Because holdings/cash are unknown, express sizing against a standard single-name weight: build toward ~1.0x before the late-July Q3 print, then scale only to ~1.2–1.4x after the print confirms the catalyst is converting to demand. Deploy ~25–30% of the intended position only on stabilization above $316 (never on first touch, and not between $320–$334), add another ~25–30% into the $301–$316 confluence on a reclaim/volume signal rather than a falling knife, and keep ~30–40% dry powder for a volume-confirmed close above $335 or post-earnings confirmation. If the caller is already above standard weight, trim into $333–$335 and hold a core; size the starter so a gap through the $299 stop stays inside the risk budget, treat a close below the 50-SMA ($301.66) on expanding volume as a pause on adds, and the 200-SMA (~$274) as thesis invalidation.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is decided by the fundamentals, structure, and catalyst; the size is decided by entry timing and event risk — and that split lands on a disciplined Overweight. The aggressive analyst carried the substantive cases and neither opponent contested them: Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.2B (+16.6%), EPS $2.01 (+21.8%), gross margin 49.3% (+230bps), H1 operating cash flow $82.6B (+53%), FCF ~$78.3B, net cash ~$61.9B with debt-to-equity falling from 1.34 to ~0.80. The trend stack is fully aligned (333.26 > 10-EMA 316.62 > 50-SMA 301.66 > rising 200-SMA 273.82; MACD 7.87 vs 4.64 signal; price above VWMA 300.72), and the China Apple Intelligence approval via Alibaba's Qwen with Baidu is a dated, regulator-cleared event that closes a specific feature-parity gap, corroborated across multiple sources. That combination rules out Underweight/Sell and rules out standing aside.

What kept this from being a full-size chase is the conservative/neutral case, which the aggressive analyst never fully answered. Entry is genuinely extended: RSI 71.43, price ~5.3% above the 10-EMA and ~10.5% above the 50-SMA, pinned at the $334.79 upper Bollinger band, ATR 8.30 (~2.5% daily) after a -12.7% three-week drawdown in late June; the $299 stop is defensible normal-day math but not gap-proof into the late-July Q3 print, which the conservative correctly frames as a binary event (IDC itself flagged China demand "pulled ahead"). The quality caveats are real and unrefuted: the +53% OCF vs +17% net income gap includes working-capital timing, R&D is up ~33.6% YoY and the tax rate is rising, ~$12.5B of intangibles moved with unclear origin, partner/concession economics on the China deals are undisclosed (permission is not yet proven demand), the 261.8M-share June flush distorts VWMA precision, and Jefferies "prefers Amazon" is a relative-preference call rather than negative evidence on Apple's figures.

Deciding between the two sizing camps: the aggressive analyst's 1.2–1.4x before a binary print is above-normal exposure to a single name at record highs with elevated ATR — too loose. The conservative analyst's 0.5–0.75x cap with post-earnings-only participation is too tight and, per our own recent AAPL reflections, has repeatedly cost 5-day alpha by letting entry mechanics quietly become underweighting (the +5.4%/+4.5%/+1.8% windows where the dip never arrived and only the starter participated). The neutral framework wins on the merits: keep the full bullish thesis, but stage capital, hold pre-Q3 at or below ~1.0x standard, buy the $316/$301–$316 confluence only on confirmation, keep dry powder for a volume-confirmed breakout above $335 or a post-Q3 report, and scale toward 1.2–1.4x only once earnings and volatility give evidence the catalyst is converting to demand.

What would change the call: a decisive close below $301.66 on expanding volume with MACD rolling negative pauses adds and moves toward Underweight; a break of the 200-SMA (~$274) invalidates the thesis and warrants exiting toward flat; Q3 gross margin rolling over from 49.3% on memory pass-through, China discount-driven share defense, or disclosure that the China/Alibaba/Baidu economics are poor — any of these shifts to Underweight. Conversely, confirmed China sell-through/upgrade data, Services reacceleration, GM holding near 49%, or resolution of the ~$12.5B intangibles and partner economics upgrades to Buy and the full 1.2–1.4x overweight. Explicit data gaps, flagged not papered over: no valuation multiples, no consensus/estimate revisions, no insider-transaction data, no China sell-through confirmation, and no disclosed partner economics — informational holes that argue for staged entry, not for avoiding the position.

**Price Target**: 345.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-underwritten at the late-July Q3 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -1.8% is mild and the window is too short to judge a 3-6 month staged-entry thesis, but it does not validate the call either. The loss undercuts the timing premise that $320–$334 should be avoided while stabilization above $316 could be bought, since price moved against the entry zone immediately rather than extending. Next time, set the first tranche deeper at the $301–$316 confluence unless volume confirms a reclaim, and pre-commit to a starter size that keeps a 5-day adverse move from costing more than a fraction of the risk budget.

[2026-07-15 | AAPL | Hold | -0.5% | +0.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL at benchmark weight. Do not add at $327.50: with only ~0.7% of room to the upper Bollinger Band ($329.83) against an ATR of $8.33 (~2.5% of price), new capital is poorly compensated, and all three risk analysts, the trader, and the research plan converge on that. Keep the core position for the reported fundamentals and stacked uptrend, stage a ~25–30% add-on reserve only on confirmed pullbacks ($313 then ~$301) or a genuine post-event breakout, and hedge ~50% of delta (or trim 10–15% into strength above $327.50) through the imminent Q3 print. Cap total exposure near benchmark to ~110–125% of standard until Q3 and the $12.5B intangibles question clear. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate splits across time horizons and, on the only actionable question — what to do with capital today — converges to Hold. The bull owns direction: Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.2B (+16.6% YoY), gross margin 49.3% (+220 bps), operating margin 32.3%, EPS $2.01 (+21.8%), ~$78.3B H1 FCF, ~$53.6B net cash, plus a technically stacked structure (price $327.50 > 10 EMA $312.92 > 50 SMA $300.53 > 200 SMA $273.43, MACD 6.60 vs 3.84 signal with expanding histogram, price above VWMA $296.42). The bear conceded none of that is broken, so the core stays — the $327.50 close the session after a KeyBanc Underweight reads as demand absorbing bad news, not distribution.

But the bear and neutral analysts win the entry, and that governs new capital. At $327.50 there is only ~0.7% upside to resistance ($329.83) against a $8.33 ATR, with RSI 68.77, +19% in three weeks, 9% above the 50 SMA and ~20% above the 200 SMA. The aggressive $296 stop is ~9.6% away (nearly four ATRs) — a wide swing stop that ignores gap risk into a binary Q3 print. The quality-of-earnings jabs survive: +53% H1 OCF flattered by working-capital swings and cash taxes of $20.4B vs $31.7B; a +$12.5B net intangibles jump alongside a 25% buyback cut ($37.0B) leaving organic-vs-acquired growth unresolved; R&D +33.6% and a tax rate of 17.5% vs 15.5% creating a plausible deceleration of EPS toward low-to-mid teens; and unrebutted KeyBanc forward worries (weaker hardware demand, slower Services, price-hike elasticity). No KeyBanc target, Q3 guidance, consensus, or 10-Q intangible footnote exists in the dataset — that absence is why the reserve must not be pre-committed.

I adopt the neutral analyst's framework over both extremes: the aggressive pre-committed breakout chase at the upper band (and 125% sizing) right before Q3 is uneconomic, while the conservative cap-at-benchmark-forever is too rigid for a name still expanding margins on a stacked uptrend. Hold is the disciplined synthesis — full exposure to a confirmed trend, no chase into resistance and a binary event, and a smaller, confirmation-gated reserve. Upgrades to Overweight on a decisive close above $329.83 on ≥70M volume with follow-through, ideally post-Q3 with Services reaccelerating and hardware holding at ~49% gross margin. Downgrades toward Underweight on a decisive break of the $296.42 VWMA on expanding volume, a combined Q3 Services/hardware miss with margin compression, or confirmation that much of the growth was acquired rather than organic; $273.43 (200 SMA) is structural invalidation.

**Price Target**: 340.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months (spanning the imminent Q3 print)

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of +0.5% (raw -0.5%) is consistent with a Hold but far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis built around the Q3 print and $340 target. The window modestly supports the entry caution — price stalled below the $329.83 upper band rather than breaking out, so declining to add at $327.50 cost nothing and the hedge/trim-into-strength advice looks early-right rather than wrong. Lesson: when upside to resistance (~0.7%) is under a third of ATR, treat the "no-add" call as a volatility trade, not a directional one, and judge it on whether the band actually caps price over the following 10–15 sessions, not 5.

[2026-07-14 | AAPL | Overweight | +4.1% | +4.6% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Own AAPL but earn the overweight in stages rather than taking the full increment at $314.86 into event risk. Build to roughly 1.05-1.10x a standard allocation pre-event: Tranche 1 of the incremental overweight near the 10-EMA ($309.68-$310) on stabilization, Tranche 2 into the $299.58-$300.40 50-SMA/mid-band confluence if it holds, and reserve the final ~0.10x plus any breakout tranche for a decisive close above $325.61 on rising volume, ideally after the late-July Q3/TSMC prints. Because prior AAPL calls show entry-price caution repeatedly cost alpha, pre-commit to at least a partial add on strength if no pullback arrives. A daily close below $300 cuts the incremental overweight back to a standard allocation; core holders keep their core.

**Investment Thesis**: The bull wins the question of whether AAPL is worth owning; the bear wins only the question of how much to pay today — hence a staged Overweight, not a Buy and not a Hold. Substance is decisive: H1 FY2026 revenue +16.1% to $254.94B (Q2 +16.6%), diluted EPS +21.8%, gross margin 48.6%/Q2 49.3%, operating margin 34.0%, ~$78.3B H1 free cash flow (~30.7% margin), ~$61.9B net cash, and record 20% global smartphone share while global Q2 shipments fell 11% — taking share and expanding margins in a shrinking market. The fully stacked trend (price $314.86 above rising 10-EMA $309.68, 50-SMA $299.58, 200-SMA $273.08 with a widening golden cross; MACD 5.474 vs signal 3.145 with expanding histogram; RSI 61.45 not overbought) confirms it, and my own record warns against letting pullback-reflex become underweighting: two prior Underweight AAPL calls (2026-06-30, 2026-07-01) were wrong as price ran straight through the resistance zones.

**Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: not provided

REFLECTION:
The +4.6% five-day alpha says the Overweight direction was right, though five sessions against an event-driven thesis keyed to the late-July Q3/TSMC prints is too short to validate the full call. What this window supports is the thesis's own admission that entry-price caution has repeatedly cost AAPL alpha — price ran rather than pulling back to the 10-EMA or 50-SMA, so Tranche 2 and the breakout tranche above $325.61 likely went unfilled and the staged build captured only part of the move. Lesson for next time: when the trend is fully stacked (rising 10/50/200-SMA, expanding MACD histogram, RSI mid-range), pre-commit a larger first tranche on strength and stop treating the pullback as the base case.

[2026-07-13 | AAPL | Underweight | +2.9% | +3.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL as a MODEST, position-dependent trim into $317–$324 strength — not an exit, not a short. Do not add at $317.31; the near-term reward/risk is genuinely poor here (only ~$6.5 / ~0.8 ATR of upside to the $323.78 upper band against ~$18.6 / ~2.3 ATR of downside to the 50-SMA at $298.71). Size the trim by book, not by dogma: trim ~10–20% if the position is right-sized, and up to ~33–50% only if it is clearly oversized or concentrated, targeting ~0.5x–0.75x of a standard allocation. Keep a core, and pre-commit a FAST re-risk on a decisive close above $323.78 on >70M volume so that entry-price discipline does not quietly become underweighting. Further reduce on a daily close below the VWMA/50-SMA cluster near $294–$299; treat a break of the 200-SMA at $272.76 as the full-thesis invalidation. Horizon 1–3 months tactical, core re-scored on the breakout or the Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is trim, but the magnitude must be small — the analysts converge on 'reduce into strength' yet the prior-record lessons cap how hard I am willing to fight a confirmed uptrend.

What rules out Sell-and-short (and anchors a retained core): the franchise is strong and the trend is genuinely confirmed, not merely rallying. Q2 FY2026 revenue +16.6%, gross margin 49.3% (+222 bps), EPS +21.8%, ~$61.9B net cash. The moving-average stack is fully bullish and rising — price $317.31 > 10-EMA $308.52 > 50-SMA $298.71 > 200-SMA $272.76 — with MACD +5.24 vs a +2.56 signal, RSI 64.2 (not overbought), and a structural tailwind in the Broadcom ~$30B chip supply deal through 2031. Nothing in the packet suggests deterioration of the franchise; a Sell/exit is not supported.

What forces the trim: at spot AAPL is ~6.2% above the 50-SMA and ~16.3% above the 200-SMA, pressing the upper Bollinger Band $323.78 after an intraday $323.45 tag, with ATR elevated to $8.09 — a two-day normal shakeout is ~$16. The June tape proved a ~14% drawdown in roughly twelve sessions, including a 261.8M-share capitulation day. The bear also lands real quality-of-growth cautions the bull underweights: H1 buybacks fell 25.3% YoY ($49.50B → $36.99B), the effective tax rate rose ~15% → ~17.5%, R&D grew 32.6% vs revenue +16.6%, and the +53% OCF growth was working-capital-flattered. Add the unquantified Apple–OpenAI trade-secret lawsuit and the fact that valuation is explicitly unavailable in the dataset, and there is no defensible case to add or hold a full position at an all-time-high extension with no multiple confirmation.

Why this is Underweight and not a heavy de-risk, and why it is a modest trim rather than the aggressive 25–50% trim: my own recent record is the decisive discipline here. The last two AAPL Underweights (2026-06-30 at ~$289, 2026-07-01 at ~$294) were both directionally wrong by ~7–8% within five days, and both were 'trim into resistance' calls made against UNCONFIRMED momentum (MACD negative, RSI neutral). The current setup is different in a way that cuts AGAINST a large trim: momentum is now confirmed bullish (MACD positive and rising, RSI 64, price above a rising 50-SMA). The prior lesson explicitly warned to give positive momentum real weight once a volume-backed close above the 50-SMA prints — it now has, and stacked. Equally important, the upper band at $323.78 is only ~0.8 ATR away; the lesson that a level within ~1.5 ATR is 'a probable break, not a rejection' argues that trimming hard into it would fight a trend likely to take it out. So I adopt the neutral analyst's calibrated framing over the aggressive/conservative 25–50% directive: trim lightly if right-sized, trim harder only if oversized, and never pre-commit the reload — require a confirmed hold/bounce with volume before re-adding near $308/$299, per the conservative analyst's correct point that a lower price alone is not evidence of stabilization.

I also reject two analyst overreaches: (1) treating the $333.49 (2x ATR) level as a protective stop for a remaining long — it is an opportunity-cost/trim-thesis invalidation trigger, not downside protection; downside risk for the retained core is defined by daily closes below the $294–$299 VWMA/50-SMA cluster. (2) The aggressive analyst's 'highest-reward path' reload schedule — a legal-headline gap can skip $308/$299 entirely, so re-entry is confirmation-gated, not price-gated.

What would change the call: a decisive close above $323.78 on >70M volume with valuation support moves this to Hold/Overweight and triggers the pre-committed fast re-risk; a daily close below the $294–$299 confluence (through the VWMA ~$294 and 50-SMA) prompts further reduction toward 0.5x; a break of the rising 200-SMA at $272.76 escalates to Sell. Data gaps flagged, not papered over: no valuation multiple, no sentiment report, no insider-transaction data, no quantified memory-cost margin impact, and no confirmed Q3 guidance — so any price target would be technical guesswork rather than thesis, and none is offered.

**Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months tactical (trim); core re-scored on a confirmed breakout above $323.78 or the Q3 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of +3.9% (raw +2.9%, roughly $317 to $326) went against the Underweight, but five sessions is too short to judge a 1–3 month tactical trim thesis. What it does undercut immediately is the trim rationale itself: the call conceded the $323.78 upper band was only ~0.8 ATR away and a "probable break, not a rejection," and that is exactly what happened — trimming into a sub-1-ATR level in confirmed momentum was the losing half of the thesis, same error as the prior two AAPL Underweights. Next time, gate the trim on an actual rejection signal (failed close, volume divergence) rather than mere proximity to resistance, or size it smaller still when MACD and the MA stack are this stacked.

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL at $315.32 — keep the core at standard allocation and put no new capital to work into the four-touch $315.4/$317.4/$316.9/$316.9 shelf, which is being pressed on ~34M shares versus a 50–75M norm with only ~1.8% headroom to the upper Bollinger band at $321.20. If the caller is already overweight, trim back to standard into $315–$317; if flat, wait for one of two triggers rather than initiating at resistance. Breakout branch: a daily close above $317 on >65M shares opens a first small tranche (~+5–10% above standard) with a hard failed-breakout exit back below $317, and a second tranche only on a successful $317 retest or a close above $321.20 on sustained volume, capped near +10–20% total. Pullback branch: scale in at the $298 confluence (50-SMA $297.77 / Bollinger-mid $298.10) only if it holds on declining volume, with the second tranche after a reclaim of the 10-EMA at $306.57; structural stop is a close below $295, hard thesis line $273.75 (June 25 low), sized against ATR $8.09 (~2.6% daily range) so no single exit costs more than a fraction of portfolio risk.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction and the entry are two different questions, and the panel only looks conflicted because it is answering both at once. On direction the bull wins outright and nothing in the packet disputes him: Q2 FY2026 revenue +16.6% YoY to $111.2B, gross margin 49.3% (+220bps), operating margin expanding ~100bps even with R&D +33%, H1 free cash flow $78.3B at ~1.15x net income, ~$62B net cash, and a fully ordered rising stack — price above the 10-EMA $306.57, 50-SMA $297.77 and 200-SMA $272.45 — with MACD 4.615 vs signal 1.894 (histogram +2.721), RSI 62.93, and a 261.8M-share June 26 reversal that defended the June 25 low at $273.75. There is no lower low, no death cross, no technical breakdown. That is why I reject the Underweight/Sell side of the debate, exactly as the last two AAPL calls should have: the 2026-06-30 Underweight (+8.3% raw) and 2026-07-01 Underweight (+7.4% raw) both mis-called a name in a primary uptrend because a nearby technical level — inside one ATR — was treated as a rejection rather than a probable break. I am not repeating that error.

On entry the bear wins, and it is the bear's narrower fight that decides the rating. The $315–$317 shelf has now been touched four times; the push into it came on 34.13M shares against a 50–75M norm, which is demand not yet proven, not a "coiled spring." Price is +15.7% above the 200-SMA and +7.6% above VWMA $293.13, Bollinger width is ~15%, and there is ~1.8% of headroom to the upper rail near $321.20 against an $8.09 ATR of daily chop. The bear also lands real blows on evidentiary quality that the aggressive analyst papers over: the ~$30B Broadcom pact is headline-only from promotional sourcing, the on-device AI "proof" is a single startup demo explicitly flagged speculative, the ~$12.8B intangible jump is unexplained capital deployment rather than confirmed AI execution, buybacks are down ~25% YoY (mechanical EPS support removed), and the effective tax rate rising 15.5%→17.5% is a factual if modest EPS drag. Most decisively, no valuation multiple was assessable anywhere in the data, so after a +15.5% YTD run nobody on this panel can prove how much growth is already in the price — and at resistance the burden of proof sits with the buyer. A caller with no position should not be invited to pay for unquantified optimism at the exact level where four prior rallies stopped.

Where I overrule the aggressive analyst: "add in two tranches up to +10–20% without hesitation" on a single 65M-share close is too much, too fast, on an unverified catalyst and with no valuation anchor. Where I overrule the conservative analyst: demanding two consecutive closes above $317 plus ~75M volume plus a retest before any add, and refusing a full allocation even at $298, is the paralysis that has cost this desk alpha in name-after-name uptrends (the 2026-07-01 AMZN lesson: the "don't add" restraint simply cost relative upside without ever being proven right). The neutral analyst's construction is the one I adopt because it solves both objections at once — a single close above $317 on >65M volume as the first trigger, but sized small, with an immediate exit back below $317 rather than a wait for the wide $295 stop. That fast-failure rule is what makes a smaller confirmation bar safe.

One added point the panel under-weighted, drawn from the 2026-06-30 lesson: the $317 trigger is only ~0.5% away, well inside one ATR of $8.09. A level that close is more likely a break than a rejection. That is precisely why I hold the full core and pre-commit real size to the breakout branch rather than drifting — but it is also why I will not pay up ahead of the print, and why the failed-breakout trim below $317, not the $295 stop, is the operative risk control on any add.

What would change the call: a daily close above $317 on >65M shares with the MACD histogram still expanding moves this to Overweight with the staged adds above; a clean rejection at $317 followed by a constructive hold of the $298 confluence on declining volume is the higher-quality accumulation entry and also moves me constructive; a closing break below $295 with expanding volume invalidates the medium-term structure toward Underweight, and a decisive break of $273.75 is the full thesis failure. Explicitly missing and not papered over: any valuation multiple (P/E, EV/FCF, forward estimates) — the single biggest hole in the bull case and the first thing to re-check before the final tranche — plus confirmed Q3 FY2026 guidance, a quantified memory-cost margin impact, actual Broadcom terms, any news coverage for July 3–8, options/IV pricing for hedging, and the caller's actual AAPL weight, cost basis and cash.

**Price Target**: 321.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months tactical (trigger-driven); 12-24 months structural
